episodes.161337: A shortwave trough progressed across the region. As a result, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across western Colorado. However, dry low levels led to gusty winds rather than heavy wetting rains with convection. Some storms generated severe wind gusts.
episodes.161339: A shortwave trough progressed across the region. As a result, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across eastern Utah. However, dry low levels led to gusty winds rather than heavy wetting rains with convection. Some storms generated severe wind gusts.
episodes.161402: Showers and thunderstorms repeatedly moved across western portions of Lauderdale and Colbert Counties on the 17th, producing widespread rainfall amounts of 3-6 over a few hours. Heavy rainfall also affected Limestone County, both downtown in Decatur, and north, along the AL/TN border again on the 18th. This led to numerous reports of flooding and flash flooding in and around Cherokee, AL, Ardmore, AL, and in Decatur, AL.
episodes.162068: As Post-Tropical Cyclone Nicholas drifted over northern Louisiana, showers and thunderstorms produced heavy rain across portions of Mississippi. Some of the storms produced localized flooding.
episodes.162265: A saturated tropical airmass (PWAT over 2 inches) combined with diurnal instability and fueled locally heavy rainfall in showers and storms that formed near a meandering trough axis across north Florida and sea breezes. Weak storm motion enabled locally heavy rainfall to form and train over areas.
episodes.162307: Temperatures were hot across West Texas ahead of a cold front. A weak dryline was also in place across the Permian Basin which provided additional lift. These conditions resulted in thunderstorms that produced wind damage in Midland County.
episodes.162663: A couple of rounds of slow moving thunderstorms impacted Thomasville with significant flash flooding on both Sep 18th and Sep 19th.
episodes.163039: Thunderstorm outflow brought severe winds to the Pocatello regional airport and power outages in Pocatello.
episodes.163105: A tropical air mass covered Alabama on September 18-19 with precipitable water values over 2 inches. An nearly stationary upper low near the Texas and Louisiana state line provided lift and instability for showers and thunderstorms across the Central Gulf States. An inverted surface trough was located along the I-20 corridor on September 18th, and provided a focus for slow moving thunderstorms that produced flash flooding across Tuscaloosa, Jefferson and Shelby counties. The upper trough moved slightly eastward on the 19th and the flooding threat shifted to areas east of I-65.
episodes.163161: Convergence within a surface trough across western Oklahoma and Kansas lead to isolated thunderstorm development during the afternoon of the 17th, with a few severe wind gusts recorded in northwestern Oklahoma.
episodes.163225: A cluster of thunderstorms resulted in isolated wind damage and hail over eastern New York on Saturday September 18, 2021.
episodes.163266: A shortwave trough moving through the region combined with a moist, unstable atmosphere promoted the development of showers and thunderstorms across south-central Arizona going into the afternoon on the 18th. Adequate shear allowed for some thunderstorms to become strong to severe, leading to multiple reports of damaging winds and dense blowing dust. Additionally, thunderstorms were capable of producing locally heavy rainfall leading to isolated flash flooding. No injuries were reported.
episodes.163322: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours on September 17th. There was one isolated flooding report in Perry County.
episodes.163323: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in the morning hours and continued into the early afternoon hours on September 18th. Significant flash flooding occurred across parts of Middle Tennessee including areas of Davidson, Putnam, Bedford and Coffee Counties.
episodes.163363: A trough of low pressure located over California moved slowly across Arizona.  Large scale lift with the trough along with daytime heating to shower and thunderstorm over portions of central Arizona.
episodes.163423: Thunderstorms moved across the Uinta Basin, producing an isolated severe wind gust.
episodes.163486: A late-season trough during the monsoon, just off the southern US coast, promoted deep southerly flow from the surface through mid levels of the troposphere. This in combination with a moisture axis extending up from Sonora and marginal afternoon instability promoted the development of isolated thunderstorms across southeast California and southwest Arizona. With just enough speed shear, a few storms trained or redeveloped over the same areas resulting in localized flooding impacts with average rainfall rates around 1 inch per hour. An isolated strong to severe storm near Desert Center produced radar estimated rainfall near 2 inches in 1 hour, leading to flash flooding.
episodes.163552: A waterspout developed in association with a convective rain shower along an island cloud line.  Weak ridging was building over the Florida Keys at the time.
episodes.163567: Remnants of tropical cyclone Nicholas over Louisiana promoted a humid air mass and diurnal convection that produced heavy rains over and near the southern Plateau.
episodes.163761: Weak upslope flow coupled with a slow moving cold front and a weak mid-level disturbance triggered storm development. But moisture was limited in the lower levels. With storms that did develop, they were aided by modest lapse rates of around 8C/km with MLCAPE values up to 1000 J/kg. There was sufficient vertical shear and buoyancy to produce up to golf ball sized hail.

events.narrative: Back window blown out of a vehicle and multiple power lines downed.
Estimated severe wind gust.
Flash flooding was reported at the intersection of Old Lee Highway and Barnes Lane in Cherokee.
Flash Flooding was reported at the intersection of North Jackson Highway and E 2nd Street.
Flash flooding reported at the intersection of North Pike and Riverton Rose Trace.

Local law enforcement reported road closures in several locations due to flash flooding. This included State Route 177, which was closed between Ragsdale Road and State Route 62. Closures reported at 1755PDT. Timing adjusted based on radar estimated rainfall. No damages or injuries were reported.

A thunderstorm produced wind damage in Midland County. The roof of a barn was blown off and powerlines were blown down. Old and new trees were blown down. This damage occurred off of County Road 1140 south of County Road 158 in Midland County. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Flooding occurred at the intersection of Wolfe Road and Dowdle Road.
A few streets were flooded in Rolling Fork.
Tom's Creek Road was flooded and impassable near Highway 438 West. One water rescue occurred.

A thunderstorm produced wind damage near Midkiff. Two unanchored construction trailers were damaged. One injury was reported. The wind was estimated to be 60 to 70 mph. The time was estimated by radar. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Patton Creek overflowed its bank in several locations in Hoover and Vestavia Hills.|Flooding occurred near the Hoover Country Club with water entering several nearby residences. At least six inches of water flowed over Highway 31 where it crossed Patton Creek in Vestavia Hills.
Six to twelve inches of water flowing across Southgate Drive in Pelham.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Craig Key To West End Of Seven Mile Bridge Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A waterspout was observed about two miles southwest of the center of Seven Mile Bridge.  The waterspout was narrow, oriented upright, and the condensation funnel cloud extended halfway from the cloud base.
Kinniard Road at Dodson Branch Road was flooded. 1999 Gainesboro Grade was also flooded with a vehicle stranded in water.
Tyne Blvd, Granny White Pike, Franklin Pike Circle, Hill Road, and Edmondson Pike north of Old Hickory Blvd were flooded and impassable in places.
Whitaker Springs Road was flooded near the Putnam County Sports Complex as well as at Fisk Road.
Country Farm Road near Pippin Road was flooded.
Belle Meade Blvd and the Belle Meade Plaza parking garage on Harding Road were flooded.
Richland Creek crested at 9.66 feet in moderate flood stage, which is the 3rd highest stage on record for this river gauge.
Sevenmile Creek was flooding Blackman Road and Nolensville Road at Edmondson Pike.

Severe flooding across the cities of Northport and Tuscaloosa.  Water was 2-3 feet deep along portions of 14th Avenue in the city of Tuscaloosa with numerous roads flooded and impassable across the city. One fatality was reported near the intersection of Greensboro Avenue and 24th Street as a vehicle was swept off the road and into a drainage ditch.
A house was reportedly flooded with vehicles floating down the creek in the 500 block of Carr Creek Road.
Flash flooding was reported in several parts of the county.
There were numerous reports of a funnel cloud near Hudson Falls.
Hickory Hills Road was flooded and impassable.
Nickel size hail was reported on Coronado Way.
A tree was reported down on Partridge Drum Road.
An AWS mesonet site measured 3.58 inches of rainfall in the past 6 hours. About 2.07 inches fell in the past hour.
Occupants of a vehicle rescued from a flooded ditch at Park Avenue in Ardmore, AL.
Idaho Power reported about 1,000 customers in Pocatello without power on the afternoon of the 18th.
ASOS at Pocatello Regional Airport recorded a thunderstorm outflow wind of 59 mph.
An isolated severe wind gust of 58 mph was recorded at Duchesne Municipal Airport.
Multiple photos on social media showed numerous power poles were knocked over west of Maricopa along Ralston Road between Highway 238 and McDavid Road. No injuries were reported.
Some evacuations were occurring primarily along Branch Road.
Multiple vehicles submerged in the floodwaters between Ardmore and Elkmont. Depth of water unknown.
A large tree estimated to be 8 to 10 inches in diameter fell in the Grand Junction city cemetery as a result of thunderstorm winds.

Multiple social media images showed a waterspout that formed over Orange Lake, just north of Citra. The waterspout persisted for about 10 minutes. All parameters were estimated, including the path width and track length and EF scale. There were no reported damage or injuries.
Barnes Road washed out in Ardmore, AL.
A tree was reported down on McClintock Drive between Elliot Road and Warner Road blocking southbound traffic. No injuries were reported.
According to the Salt River Project (SRP), a power pole was blown over near Main Street and Dobson Road. No injuries were reported.
A peak wind gust of 58 MPH was measured by the automated weather station at the Grand Junction Regional Airport.
A peak wind gust of 58 MPH was measured by the automated weather station at the Canyonlands Field Airport.
Lee Street in front of the Courthouse is under water. Parts of Church Street also underwater, affecting businesses. Fire and Police Dept assisting motorists in the area. Depth of water unknown.

Video on social media showed part of Highway 238 appearing to be impassable between mile posts 33-35 due to flooding. The Arizona Department of Public Safety (DPS) also responded to a vehicle stalled due to flooding in this area. No injuries were reported.

There were at least 15 vehicles stranded in flood waters in Thomasville.  Police had to enter flood waters to rescue citizens from stalled vehicles.  Significant street flooding occurred across Thomasville with water up to at least one building.

Granite Creek in Prescott (GCRA3) rose around 4.15 feet between 445 PM and 615 PM. The waster began to decrease after 700 PM.  A video posted on social media showed ongoing flooding in Granite Creek Park a mile north of Prescott Courthouse at 632 PM.
Flooding, especially near Branch Road, was ongoing but improving.
A peak wind gust of 63 MPH was measured by the automated weather station at the Rifle Garfield County Regional Airport.
